_comment: Azure-only Stado deployment. Install at ~/.config/stado/config.json (or point $STADO_CONFIG at it). Resolution order is env > this file > built-in default, so deploy/azure/env.example still overrides anything here. Replace every <placeholder> before use; empty strings are treated as unset and fall through to the built-in default, which is GCP-shaped.

gcs._comment: Not used for routing under the azure backend, but queue/storage.rs keeps it as bucket_name and it leaks into gs:// URIs (machine.rs) and the coverage verifier. Keep it matching the container name.

azure._network_comment: The provider does NOT create networking. vnet and nsg must already exist per region, named <vnet>-<location> and <nsg>-<location> (providers/azure/network.rs). The subnet is a child of the region vnet so it carries no suffix.
azure._image_comment: image_urn is omitted so the built-in default applies: the microsoft-dsvm ubuntu-hpc image, which ships the NVIDIA driver and CUDA preinstalled. Override here only to pin a different publisher:offer:sku:version.

release._comment: Binary release channel for self-update and for the agent VM bootstrap. The built-in default is the GCS releases bucket, which is dead with GCP billing off. Mirror releases/stado/** into the Azure container and point this at it, or no agent VM can install itself.

alerts._comment: Empty topic disables the GCP Pub/Sub channel; left at its default it is non-empty, so every alert pays a failing ADC probe before falling through. Slack/Telegram/SendGrid are unaffected — configure at least one or alerting is silently gone.
